title: Adaptive session-based backoff with idempotency propagation and hedged-fanout guidelines
creator: Maya Sanchez
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, cross-service standard for retry/timeouts/backoff that adapts per-session workload characteristics, ensures safe idempotency propagation across retries and hedged requests, and prescribes hedged-fanout and load-shedding behavior for high-latency regimes. This ticket covers the spec, SDK contract changes, server-side runtime knobs, and a measurable rollout plan. Motivation: Incidents in the last 6 months showed cascading retries and amplified tail latency during multi-region failovers. We need a single resiliency primitive that services can adopt without custom per-team rules while allowing SLO-driven tuning.
acceptance_criteria: A concise spec document (<=4 pages) describing session lifecycle, adaptive backoff algorithm, idempotency semantics, hedged-fanout guardrails, and load-shedding triggers.

SDK changes: new RetryPolicy v2 API across main languages with fields: session_id, session_ttl_ms, adaptive_backoff_config, hedging_config, idempotency_key_propagation. Backwards-compatible overloads must exist.

Runtime integration: runtime exposes per-route knobs (max_concurrency, target_p95_ms, hedge_allowed=true/false) and implements server-side enforcement of hedged request deduplication using idempotency metadata.
End-to-end tests and canary demonstrating reduced excess retries and stable p99 during a simulated regional outage in staging.
Dashboards: per-service metrics for retry amplification, hedged hit/miss rate, idempotency deduplication rate, dropped_requests due to load-shedding.
Runbook entry created that describes when to disable hedging or alter session_ttl.
Security review completed for idempotency key storage/propagation and replay protections.
implementation_plan: Design doc: publish to Confluence and add to proposal PR (linked below).
Spec review: sync with SDK owners (python, typescript, go) and runtime team; collect feedback in the doc and iterate.
SDK: implement RetryPolicy v2 shims that map to existing clients; add session headers and idempotency propagation helper.
Runtime: add hedged-fanout routing middleware that observes session_id and uses a short dedupe window keyed by idempotency signature.
Tests: unit tests for dedupe logic, integration tests for hedged requests, chaos tests for failover scenarios.
Canary: enable new policy for a low-traffic tenant and monitor metrics for 72 hours before expanding.
Rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
Docs: update SDK docs and add migration guide for teams using custom retry logic.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): full stack test with synthetic traffic generator — validate dedupe and latency improvements.
Phase 1 (canary): pick three small services (internal infra, experiments, search) for 10% traffic pass-through with hedging enabled.
Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 30% and 60% with 24-hour observation windows; manual check-in at each step.
Phase 3 (full): enable as default policy for new services; existing services opt-in or schedule migrations.
Rollback criteria: sustained p99 latency increase > 15% over baseline for 30 minutes or error rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
monitoring_and_metrics: retry_amplification_ratio: ratio of total attempts to original requests (goal: <=1.5 in normal ops).
hedge_trigger_rate: percentage of requests that spawn hedged attempts.
hedge_success_rate: fraction where the hedged attempt returned first and was accepted (informative, target 20-50% in high-tail workloads).
idempotency_dedup_rate: fraction of duplicate attempts deduplicated server-side (should be low except during failovers).
load_shed_count: requests intentionally dropped due to backpressure with reason codes.
slo_p95_latency and slo_p99_latency tracked per-route during rollout.
open_questions: What is the canonical idempotency token format? Proposal: sha256(service||route||client_provided_key||body_prefix) hex with 64-bit timestamp truncated — feedback requested.
How large should server-side dedupe windows be per model size / route? Default 2s for short-lived requests, 10s for long-running inference — needs validation.
Do we allow cross-region dedupe state replication? Costly — initial plan: best-effort local dedupe with hedging hints to downstream regions.
Should hedging be allowed for non-idempotent mutate endpoints? Default: off unless explicit safe-mode annotated.
